methodological_rigor.justification: Design is a randomized, open-label, parallel-group phase II trial with a 3+3 safety run-in and 1:1 randomization in 55 patients, with a pre-specified sample size calculation (n=25 per arm providing 80% power at two-sided alpha=0.1 to detect a 20% pCR increase over a 15% historical control). Strengths include pre-specified ITT/mITT/safety analysis sets, a CONSORT-style flow, and biomarker pre-planning (PD-L1/TIGIT/PVR). Key limitations: the primary efficacy claim rests on comparison to historical controls rather than head-to-head between arms (Methods explicitly state 'No formal comparisons were made between the two experiment arms'), the significance level is lenient (alpha=0.1), the trial is open-label with no stated allocation concealment or blinded central pathology review, and the historical control pCR of 15% is anchored to two older references without a sensitivity analysis against more contemporary controls. The small per-arm sample (~27) is underpowered for the biomarker and subgroup analyses, as the authors acknowledge.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual randomized phase II trial, but because the primary efficacy inference relies on historical rather than randomized comparison and the trial is small, open-label, with lenient alpha, it functions as a low-quality RCT consistent with Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is high: LARC with pMMR/MSS biology has been largely refractory to immunotherapy, and achieving pCR of 35.7% with Atezo+Tira after nCRT (vs 15% historical, p=0.002) with a manageable grade 3-4 TRAE rate (31%) is clinically meaningful and nominates a novel neoadjuvant backbone. pCR remains a surrogate endpoint and median follow-up is only 21.55 months with no deaths yet, so translational impact depends on maturation of EFS/RFS/OS data; still, the combination (TIGIT + PD-L1 after nCRT in MSS rectal cancer) is directly relevant to ongoing phase III development.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT applies given the randomized parallel-group design. The manuscript reports trial registration (NCT05009069), IRB approval, pre-specified inclusion/exclusion criteria, a CONSORT-style flow diagram (Fig 1), analysis sets (ITT, mITT, safety), primary and secondary endpoints, and detailed AE reporting with CTCAE grading. Omissions: randomization sequence generation, allocation concealment, stratification factors, and whether pathologic review was blinded are not described; a formal protocol/SAP appendix is not referenced; the historical-control derivation is thin. No explicit data-sharing or code-availability statement is present in the manuscript text, consistent with a 2 for reproducibility posture (methods are reproducible in outline but patient-level data and analytic code are not offered).

novelty_literature.justification: Novelty is primarily empirical and populational: this is positioned as the first randomized phase II to evaluate dual TIGIT + PD-L1 blockade (tiragolumab + atezolizumab) following long-course nCRT in LARC, specifically in pMMR/MSS tumors where immunotherapy response has been limited. Prior work provides direct comparators that temper the novelty: R-IMMUNE (Atezo + nCRT, 24% pCR), VOLTAGE-A (nivolumab + nCRT), AVANA (avelumab + nCRT), UNION (camrelizumab + SCRT), and Xu/Xiao et al. (sintilimab + nCRT), as well as CITYSCAPE and MORPHEUS-Liver establishing the Atezo+Tira combination outside rectal cancer. The incremental step - adding anti-TIGIT in the neoadjuvant rectal setting - is meaningful but builds on an established scaffold rather than defining a new paradigm.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a clear IMRaD structure; the abstract is quantitatively grounded and faithful to the results. Methods are detailed on eligibility, treatment schedule, endpoints, immunohistochemistry assays, and analysis sets; results are presented with CIs and p-values. The discussion is appropriately cautious about cross-trial comparisons, acknowledges the pCR surrogate controversy (RAPIDO 5-year local recurrence), and enumerates concrete limitations. Minor issues: some sentences are dense (e.g., mechanistic paragraph on RT-immune synergy), the historical-control justification could be sharper, and a few acronyms (TIC, IC) are introduced with minimal signposting; captions for Fig 1/2 are informative.

key_strengths: First randomized phase II to evaluate dual TIGIT + PD-L1 blockade (atezolizumab + tiragolumab) after long-course nCRT in LARC, in an all pMMR/MSS cohort where immunotherapy benefit has been elusive
Pre-specified sample size, primary endpoint (pCR), ITT/mITT/safety sets, and CONSORT-style flow with trial registration (NCT05009069)
Clinically meaningful signal: pCR 35.7% (95% CI 18.6-55.9) in Atezo+Tira vs 15% historical control (p=0.002), with 100% R0 resection and acceptable grade 3-4 TRAEs (31.0%)
Pre-planned biomarker evaluation (PD-L1, TIGIT, PVR) with defined scoring thresholds and standardized assay platforms
Transparent limitations discussion covering short follow-up, small sample, surrogate-endpoint caveats, and unassessed confounders
key_concerns: Primary efficacy inference rests on comparison to a 15% historical control anchored to two older references, with no formal between-arm statistical comparison and a lenient alpha=0.1
Open-label design with no reported allocation concealment, stratification factors, or blinded central pathology review, raising detection/performance bias risk for the pCR endpoint
Median follow-up only 21.55 months with no deaths; EFS/RFS claims are immature and surrogacy of pCR for OS in nCRT+immunotherapy is unproven
Biomarker and subgroup analyses are underpowered given per-arm n ~27, limiting predictive-biomarker claims for PD-L1/TIGIT/PVR
No explicit data-sharing or analytic-code statement; protocol/SAP not provided as supplement in the blinded text
Historical control derivation lacks sensitivity analysis against more contemporary controls (e.g., TNT era pCR ~28% in RAPIDO/PRODIGE 23), which could soften the magnitude of the apparent benefit
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically competent, well-reported small randomized phase II with a genuinely novel immunotherapy combination (Atezo + Tira after nCRT) in MSS LARC and a clinically meaningful pCR signal, but limited by historical-control-based inference, open-label design, and immature survival data; this profile fits tier 2 (specialist/translational oncology journals) with minor revisions rather than a top-tier practice-changing venue.
